title: The last teaching
hook: Milarepa shows his student Gampopa the callouses from years of sitting: that is the secret

segments.voice: Yesterday, Milarepa in his cave, green from the nettles and singing anyway. Your line was green from nettles. How did your simple meal taste? Day nine hundred seventy-five.

A goodbye at a river crossing. The old man has walked his student partway down the road. The student, Gampopa, has trained with him, and now he's being sent off to practice and teach on his own. They say their farewells. The student bows. Then Milarepa calls him back. Wait, he says, in the story. I have one more instruction, a very precious one. I wasn't sure I'd give it to you. Gampopa turns around, ready for the deepest secret of all. Today: Milarepa.
screen: `A GOODBYE AT THE RIVER.` → `WAIT. ONE MORE.` → `THE DEEPEST SECRET?`

segments.voice: First, the reveal. Milarepa turns his back to Gampopa, hitches up his robe, and shows him his backside. It is covered in thick calluses, hard as hide, from sitting on stone for years. And he says, in effect: this is it. There's no instruction more profound than this. Practice. Sit until your seat looks like mine. Second, the joke. It is funny, and it's meant to be. The great master, the singer of the mountains, keeps his most precious teaching for last, and it's his rear end. It's hard to retell without a grin. Third, the point under the joke. Everything Milarepa had, he got from teachings he received and then practiced, again and again, alone, in cold caves. The teaching mattered. But a teaching that isn't practiced is a map left folded in a drawer. The calluses are what reading the map looks like after years on the road. Fourth, why it's the last one. A student leaving a teacher wants a key, a secret, something to keep in a pocket. Milarepa gives Gampopa the opposite of a shortcut. The secret is that there's no secret, only the long sitting. Some hear good news in that. Nothing is being held back. There's no hidden password. There's only showing up, and showing up again. Tomorrow, we follow the student who walked away from that river carrying it.
screen: `HE SHOWS HIS CALLUSES.` · `IT'S MEANT TO BE FUNNY.` · `A MAP LEFT IN A DRAWER.` · `THE SECRET: NO SHORTCUT.` · then, large: `THAT'S THE SECRET.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: sit a little longer. Settle, and breathe. Feel where your body meets the seat, the weight, the pressure, the contact. That's where Milarepa's secret lives. Stay with the breath. And when the bell rings, don't jump up. Give it a few extra breaths, just a little longer than you'd like, and let that be the whole teaching for today. The bell holds the time.
Milarepa. The singer of the mountains, whose parting gift to his student Gampopa was his calluses from years of sitting, and no secret beyond practice. Today's word.
Your line: that's the secret. Today, when you want a shortcut for something that matters, smile, and just do the next bit of the work. Day nine hundred seventy-five.

howItsDone: Tibetan teachers tell the story of Milarepa's last teaching to Gampopa, often with humor, to stress that steady practice matters more than any secret instruction.

fork.setup: you're Milarepa, saying goodbye to your student. you have one last thing to give him. what is it?
options: a secret text no one else has seen.
a blessing that guarantees his awakening.
a look at your calluses from years of sitting.
fork.reveal: Milarepa showed Gampopa his callused backside: there's no secret beyond practice.

trapdoor: what you thought: a strange, slightly rude joke.
what it means: the most precious instruction is to practice, for years, without a shortcut.
what a scholar hears: the parting scene of the master-disciple story, turning the hunger for secret teaching into a call to sit.
